=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture

B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single blade attached to the stem)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology

    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (leaves are significantly longer than wide, widest below the middle, tapering to a point)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acuminate (the leaf tip tapers to a slender point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (the leaf base tapers to the petiole, appearing wedge-shaped)

    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (the petioles are visible but relatively short compared to the leaf blade length)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (the petioles appear cylindrical and rounded in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (the stem appears green and flexible, lacking the thick, brown, corky appearance of a woody stem)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (the stem surface appears smooth)
    19. Stem color: green (the visible stem is green)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (the stem surface appears even without ridges or prominent lenticels)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules are clearly visible at the leaf bases)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
